headline.caveat: Initial Aug 2025 leases: >200MW critical IT load at Lake Mariner (NY) over 10 years; ~$8.7B including two 5-year extension options. Subsequent expansions (CB-5 +160MW and later phases) lift contracted totals to ~$6.7B base / ~$16B with extensions per FY26 disclosures.

realized_to_date.caveat: First buildings delivering in 2026 (CB-1/CB-2 from 1H26, CB-5 from 2H26); lease revenue has begun but cumulative payments are not broken out.

nature_md: Fluidstack leases purpose-built AI data-center capacity (>360MW total contracted across WULF-1/WULF-2/CB-5) at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner campus in western New York under ~10-year triple-net-style hosting leases with extension options. Fluidstack is the tenant of record serving the Google/Anthropic compute stack; Google backstops a large share of Fluidstack's lease obligations and took TeraWulf equity (see related backstop edge). Converts a bitcoin-mining site into contracted AI infrastructure.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Fluidstack (private; no public financials) takes on multi-billion long-term lease obligations — capitalized as ROU assets/lease liabilities under IFRS16/ASC842 in its own books — against end-customer compute contracts. Its thin balance sheet is exactly why Google's credit support was required.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: TeraWulf books contracted lease/hosting revenue from each building's service start (2026+) and finances construction with project debt made bankable by the Google backstop; contracted revenue re-rated the equity from a miner to an AI landlord.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** long-tenor contracted revenue with credit enhancement from Google — the cleanest miner-to-AI conversion trade. **Bear:** the direct counterparty is a thinly-capitalized private intermediary; the structure works only because of Google's contingent support, concentrating everything on one guarantor's continued appetite.

events.title: Fluidstack exercises CB-5 expansion (+160MW) at Lake Mariner
